name: morpheos
title: MorpheOS — today
lede: An operating system built on one promise — never breaks, and heals itself — whose unbreakable wedge is already real in a virtual machine: measured, tested, and now graduating onto a real laptop.
sub: This page is the results in one read — what is real and measured, and what is honestly not built yet.

callout: The boundary that matters: "VM-proven" means a CI job boots it and reads the verdict off the disk. It does not mean it has run on a person's machine. Say "builds" or "VM-proven" — never "works" — until a person has sat at it.
where: ADR 0014 ("express road first") re-sequenced the plan around one exit: a general user boots a laptop, gets online, browses, and cannot make the machine unbootable. The hard part — the unbreakable wedge — is already built and VM-proven; what's left is finishing the shell, then proving the whole stack on one real laptop. Every other dream (capsules, the AI layer, the mesh) stays in a widening backlog — none dropped, all gated behind a machine a person can actually use.
